issues.description: Naming inconsistency: command pair uses plural form while sibling commands use singular (smuggled inconsistency in the public command surface)
issues.detail: Existing commands are named `quickmark_save`, `bookmark_load`, `quickmark_add` — singular. The new commands are `quickmarks_reload` and `bookmarks_reload` — plural. The author cannot state a rule that distinguishes the two conventions; they have simply written what felt natural. A command vocabulary that cannot be derived from a stated rule is a vocabulary that will accrete contradictions. State the rule, or rename to `quickmark_reload` / `bookmark_reload`.

issues.description: Precondition on `reload()` is unstated: behavior under concurrent save/load and under malformed on-disk content is undefined (UNREASONED)
issues.detail: The `reload()` method has no documented precondition. What if the file is being written by the save-manager at the moment of reload? What if a line is malformed mid-file? The previous constructor path was equally undisciplined, but factoring it out makes the contract a public one. The author should state: precondition (file exists or is absent — both legal), postcondition (`self.marks` equals exactly the parsed contents of the file at some point during the call; `changed` was emitted exactly once), frame (only `self.marks` and `self._lineparser` may change). Without this, callers cannot reason.

issues.description: `changed` signal semantics altered without analysis: reload now emits one signal for clear-plus-repopulate where the old constructor emitted none
issues.detail: The constructor previously populated `self.marks` silently — no `changed.emit()` during init. The new `reload()` calls `self.marks.clear()` (which does not emit, because it bypasses the public `clear()` method that does emit) and then emits `changed` once at the end. This is probably the right choice, but it is a behavior change that should have been reasoned about and stated. Subscribers to `changed` who assumed marks only grow or shrink by single entries may observe a whole-table swap. State the invariant: `changed` is emitted exactly once per reload, after `self.marks` reflects the new on-disk state.

issues.description: Bypassing the public `clear()` method inside `reload()` smuggles a second clear-semantics into the class
issues.detail: The class already has a `clear()` method (lines 99-101 in the original) that does `self.marks.clear(); self.changed.emit()`. `reload()` instead calls `self.marks.clear()` directly to suppress the intermediate emit. Now there are two ways to empty `self.marks` with different signal behavior. Either factor out a private `_clear_silent()` with a documented contract, or call `clear()` and accept the double-emit and document why. Two undocumented clear-paths in one class is exactly the kind of accreted complexity that defeats reasoning.

issues.description: `_init_lineparser()` is called twice across the object lifetime with no stated idempotence contract
issues.detail: Construction calls `reload()`, which calls `_init_lineparser()`. A later `reload()` call invokes `_init_lineparser()` again. Whether the LineParser is safe to re-instantiate on the same path mid-flight is unstated. Either document that `_init_lineparser` is idempotent and re-entrant, or have `reload()` reuse the existing parser. The author has not reasoned about which.

issues.description: Tests are TESTED-NOT-PROVED and miss the interesting cases
issues.detail: The unit test demonstrates one happy-path reload. The end-to-end tests assert only that an info message appears. None of: (a) reload after the file is deleted, (b) reload with a malformed line, (c) reload mid-save, (d) reload that produces no change emits `changed` zero or one times — a decision the author has not made. Per the maxim: tests show the presence of bugs, not their absence. The author has produced evidence that the function does *something*, not that it does the right thing.

The two new Gherkin scenarios are introduced with bare `Scenario:` lines and no descriptive title, unlike every other scenario in the file. A scenario that cannot be named is a scenario whose specification the author has not stated. Add `Scenario: Reloading bookmarks` / `Scenario: Reloading quickmarks`.

issues.description: Command name in feature file (`bookmarks-reload`, `quickmarks-reload`) versus Python identifier (`bookmarks_reload`) — verify the dash/underscore mapping is the convention
issues.detail: qutebrowser's command registration maps underscores to dashes by convention, so this is likely correct, but the author should have stated it. A reader of the diff cannot verify the mapping without leaving the diff.

issues.description: No documentation update for the new commands
issues.detail: qutebrowser ships generated command documentation. A new top-level command added without a doc/help update is a command whose specification exists only in the source. The author should have stated where the command is documented to end users.

review.summary: The change is small and the intent is unobjectionable, but it is UNREASONED in the technical sense. The author has not stated the precondition, postcondition, or frame of the new public `reload()` method, has not stated the `changed`-signal invariant the method now establishes, and has introduced a second clear-path that bypasses the existing `clear()` method without naming the new contract. The command-naming convention is silently broken (singular elsewhere, plural here) because no rule was stated to derive from. The tests are TESTED-NOT-PROVED: one happy-path unit test and two trivial e2e message-assertions, none of which exercise the interesting cases (missing file, malformed content, concurrent save, no-op reload). Verdict: not REFUSED — the underlying refactor is sensible and the feature is wanted — but the author must state the contract of `reload()`, reconcile the dual clear-paths, fix the naming, and add tests for the cases that would actually exercise the invariant before this is merged.
